speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for providing that history. To better understand the cause of your chronic diarrhea and lower abdominal discomfort, have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; the relief of symptoms after defecation and mucus suggest inflammatory bowel disease or infectious colitis. Given the recent camping trip and another ill camper, could you tell me if you have noticed any fever or unintended weight loss? REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, C_Reactive_Protein, Stool_Culture_and_Ova_and_Parasites.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal blood work and inflammatory markers make an acute severe bacterial infection less likely. Have you experienced any joint pain, eye redness, or a family history of inflammatory bowel disease? REQUEST TEST: Calprotectin, Celiac_Serology. REQUEST IMAGES: Colonoscopy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The elevated calprotectin confirms intestinal inflammation, and the negative celiac serology rules out celiac disease. Based on the history of mucus, urgency, and incomplete evacuation relieved by defecation, do you have any known autoimmune conditions or a family history of inflammatory bowel disease? REQUEST IMAGES: Please review the colonoscopy report for findings such as skip lesions, ulcerations, or granulomas.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ulcerative Colitis. The combination of chronic bloody/mucoid diarrhea, urgency, tenesmus (incomplete evacuation), elevated calprotectin, and relief of pain after defecation strongly points to inflammatory bowel disease, specifically Ulcerative Colitis given the continuous nature of symptoms and lack of granulomas.
